pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam paired with severe hyponatremia, urine that darkens to a port-wine color when exposed to light, and rapid neuro-psychiatric collapse precipitated by fasting (keto diet) and a cytochrome P450-inducing drug (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (HMBS), an essential enzyme in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Starvation/fasting and porphyrogenic medications upregulate hepatic delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase-1 (ALAS1). Due to the enzymatic bottleneck at HMBS, neurotoxic heme precursors—specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—accumulate massively. These toxic precursors cause central, peripheral, and autonomic demyelination and axonal damage, as well as hypothalamic dysfunction leading to SIADH and profound hyponatremia.
